_comment: Shared fixture for the answer-collapse parity tests. Python drives it from tests/unit/test_answer_collapse.py, JavaScript from tests/jest/display-logic-collapse.test.js. Both must produce `expected` for every case, or the browser and the export can disagree about whether a conditional question was shown. Add a case here rather than to either test.

cases.name: multiselect collapses to every selected label
cases.why: GH #167 follow-up (a): the frontend stores {label: label}, so no entry looked selected and a `contains` condition evaluated against one arbitrary member.

cases.name: multiselect with one selection stays scalar
cases.why: So an existing `operator: equals` on a single-ticked multiselect keeps working.

cases.name: free_response does not out-vote the chosen option
cases.why: GH #167 follow-up (b): radio's has_free_response stores a second label on the same schema.

cases.name: same label recorded twice dedupes to one answer
cases.why: GH #167 follow-up (c): a question repeated across two survey pages became ['Yes','Yes'] server-side but 'Yes' in the browser, so the condition failed server-side only and the answer was dropped from the export.

cases.name: text schema passes its value through
empty text yields nothing to compare
likert collapses to the scale point label, not the input value
cases.why: A likert's value diverges from its label under key_value / sequential_key_binding, so the label name is the stable identity.

cases.name: unknown annotation type still collapses a selection
